newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir's new state chief escapes bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir's new state chief escapes bomb attack.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas tried to kill the newly elected chief minister of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state with a bomb on Thursday, police and witnesses said on Thursday.
A Kashmiri separatist group claimed responsibility for detonating the bomb minutes before Farooq Abdullah reached his father's grave in Srinagar to pay homage on his 91st birth anniversary.
"A bomb went off near the outer wall of the graveyard," a police official told Reuters.
The explosion came a day after the state leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) escaped a bomb attack during a political rally in Kulgam town, 65 km (40 miles) south of Srinagar.
Witnesses said Thursday's explosion was 25 metres (yards) from the graveyard.

"Our militants exploded a powerful bomb near Sheikh Abdullah's grave which was targeted to kill traitor Farooq Abdullah," the pro-Pakistan Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen said in a statement circulated to newspaper offices in Srinagar, the summer capital of the Himalayan state.
"Such attacks will continue on Farooq and on his men," the group said. "We will continue our struggle till Kashmiri freedom movement reaches its logical end."
Jamiat is one of dozens of Kashmiri groups fighting for the region's merger with neighbouring Pakistan.

Abdullah, leader of Kashmir's pro-India National Conference party, was named chief minister in October after his party won a sweeping majority in the state's first assembly polls since a violent separatist revolt broke out in 1990.
A cabinet colleague Mohideen Shah was addressing a gathering at the graveyard when the bomb went off, witnesses said.
"The elements bent upon mischief are still alive and we need to remain cautious against them," Abdullah later told the gathering after laying a wreath at the grave.
The National Conference party was observing the birth anniversary of Sheikh Abdullah, Kashmir's first chief minister, who ruled the state for more than 20 years.
Also on Thursday, militants killed one paramilitary trooper and injured five others in Srinagar, police said.
They said militants lobbed a grenade and opened fire on a paramilitary bunker near a hospital.
More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990 when simmering discontent against Indian rule erupted into armed revolt.
India accuses Pakistan of training and arming Kashmir's Moslem militants, a charge denied by Islamabad.
